transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-18
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Kara Patel (StratusCore CTO), Jamal O'Neal (Lead ML Eng), Priya Rao (Head of Security)

Auto-generated Summary: quick discovery on hosting fit and benchmark plan.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Lin: hey everybody, thanks for making time, um i'm maya from redwood inference, joining today is diego our systems eng, do you want to quick intro?
[00:10] Diego Ramos: yeah hi all, diego here, se, i'll be helping with the perf and private deploy bits.
[00:20] Kara Patel: thanks, kara here — CTO. we run a mix of openai hosted for production and v-l-m locally for batch. we're exploring options to reduce per token cost and get more predictable latency.
[00:35] Jamal O'Neal: hi jamal, lead ml eng, mainly responsible for inference infra and the TGI experiments. we've got a bunch of models—some open models, some custom fine-tunes.
[00:45] Priya Rao: priya from security, i'll flag compliance and key mgmt questions.
[00:52] Maya Lin: great — high level, we wanted to understand three things: current stack + pain points, security/compliance constraints, and what success for a POC looks like.
[01:05] Kara Patel: sure — quick stack: prod is openai for chat completions, edge cases run on v-l-m (vLLM) on azure vms. cost spiked Q1 when usage doubled; tail latency is also pretty variable. we're considering hosted for simplicity, but worried about egress and data residency.
[01:30] Diego Ramos: when you say tail, are we talking 95th or 99th percentile?
[01:35] Jamal O'Neal: 95p is around 420ms for our 2k token prompts, 99p sometimes hits 1.1s depending on load and sequence lengths.
[01:45] Maya Lin: ok that's useful. our dedicated pools can give tighter SLOs and reserved throughput; private (VPC / on-prem) gives you control for KMS and network egress.
[01:58] Priya Rao: security — we need SOC two type ii, SSO with SAML, RBAC, customer-managed K M S / H S M possibilities, and audit logs for all token-level usage. any of that possible?
[02:12] Diego Ramos: yes on all — we support SOC 2 compliance documents, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC, and for private we can integrate with your KMS or HSM. hosted customers can use a managed KMS option but we can discuss a bring-your-own-key flow for dedicated.
[02:30] Kara Patel: good. another point: we run TGI for some models and vllm for low-latency paths. compatibility worries me — how much work to port?
[02:42] Maya Lin: in many cases models run with minimal changes; runtime differences are mostly around kv cache and certain custom kernels. diego, can you talk about compatibility footguns?
[02:50] Diego Ramos: yeah — common hiccups: tokenizer mismatch, custom ops compiled for a specific runtime, and quantization differences. vllm saved kv cache patterns sometimes need adaptation; TGI adapters are usually straightforward but we always validate end-to-end. fragrance of, uh, some ops show up as unknown symbols in our logs, but we have a model onboarding flow.
[03:12] Jamal O'Neal: so we care about eval parity — identical outputs for our eval set. how do you approach that?
[03:20] Maya Lin: we run an eval parity process — baseline run on your current stack, then run on a Redwood variant (hosted/dedicated/private) with same model artifact and tokenizer. we measure token-level diffs and human eval on a small sample to check for regressions.
[03:35] Kara Patel: timeline — we need something in 6 weeks for an exec review. is that realistic?
[03:42] Diego Ramos: yes for a focused POC: week 1 onboarding & data transfer, week 2 baseline runs, week 3 tuning and perf runs, week 4 security review and exec report. tight but doable.
[03:55] Priya Rao: what's the data residency story? we have EU users and want logs and PII kept in eu region.
[04:02] Maya Lin: we can pin region routing and store logs in EU region for dedicated and private. hosted api can be region-restricted as well — we'll note specifics in the security docs.
[04:15] Jamal O'Neal: cost — curious about per-token deltas vs openai and how batching/caching could help. we use lots of prefix caching in vllm for sessions.
[04:28] Diego Ramos: our optimize toolkit proposes batching and prefix/KV caching; when you have sticky sessions we can reduce per-token compute by up to 30-40% depending on distribution. cost comparison depends on model family and quantization. we'll include a cost model.
[04:45] Kara Patel: for the POC we want 95p latency under 500ms for our typical 1.5k token cases and cost within 20% of current.
[04:55] Maya Lin: good concrete target. we'll aim to define the benchmark with your prompt set.
[05:03] Jamal O'Neal: one technical thing — we use custom CUDA kernels in some places for faster attention. does redwood support kernel selection or custom ops?
[05:12] Diego Ramos: we have a compilation layer that picks kernels based on hw and sequence length. for private we can bring in custom ops but need to vet and reproduce — it's part of the onboarding.
[05:25] Kara Patel: network egress: do you support keeping raw logs in our VPC?
[05:30] Maya Lin: for private yes, logs stay inside your VPC. for dedicated we offer options to forward logs to your storage. hosted will store logs in our secure storage with region controls and export options.
[05:45] Priya Rao: would need an audit trail for token access and a way to prove we didn't leak data — can you produce tamper-evident logs?
[05:53] Diego Ramos: yes we support append-only audit logs with export and hashing; for private you can route to your KMS-backed log store.
[06:05] Kara Patel: curious about rollout strategy — can we do canary to reduce risk?
[06:10] Maya Lin: absolutely — we support canary rollouts, A/B, automatic fallback to another model variant when quality or latency breaches thresholds.
[06:22] Jamal O'Neal: ok so POC scope: run eval parity, perf baselines, cost model, and security sign-off.
[06:30] Maya Lin: exactly. i'll share a benchmark playbook and a template to capture your traffic mix. diego will send detailed perf commands (docker/cli) so you can run locally or let us run against hosted.
[06:45] Kara Patel: we prefer you run a hosted baseline first using our prompt set, low friction, then if good we try a dedicated pilot.
[06:53] Maya Lin: sounds good. any blockers now?
[06:57] Priya Rao: one: encryption in transit and at rest must be proven for the POC. second: SAML integration timeline — we need SP metadata.
[07:08] Diego Ramos: we'll add TLS cert details and a SAML metadata example in the security packet.
[07:15] Jamal O'Neal: another small thing — do you support model pinning and automatic fallback to open model variants?
[07:22] Maya Lin: yes, model pinning and fallback policies exist so you can point to a specific artifact and have defined fallback chains.
[07:30] Kara Patel: okay let's talk scheduling — i'm out next week but team can receive artifacts. prefer kickoff the week after.
[07:37] Maya Lin: we'll target the week of Apr 26 for onboarding. we'll send the benchmark template today.
[07:45] Diego Ramos: i'll include perf script examples (vllm and tgi compatible) and a note where tokenizer mismatches frequently occur.
[07:55] Priya Rao: please include the specific KMS questions — we use AWS KMS and an H S M for key wrapping.
[08:03] Maya Lin: noted. we'll prepare the security questionnaire and an architectural doc for private deployment.
[08:15] Jamal O'Neal: one more — how do you handle model version rollbacks if a new model regresses?
[08:22] Diego Ramos: we support version pinning and quick rollbacks; also automatic regression alerts tied to eval sets so you can revert within minutes.
[08:30] Kara Patel: perfect.
[08:32] Maya Lin: recap and next steps: i'll send pricing/workflow + benchmark template; diego sends perf scripts and a compatibility note; priya will send security requirements and SSO metadata; kara/jamal will provide prompt set and traffic mix.
[08:48] Kara Patel: ok thanks everyone.
[08:51] Maya Lin: thank you — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the onboarding week.
[08:58] (call ends)

--- End transcript ---

Notes: Transcript contains casual speech and occasional ASR errors (e.g., 'v-l-m' vs vLLM, 'K M S' spelled out). References to decks and security artifacts to be shared as links in follow-up email.
